messages:
maria: Ran a quick nsys timeline on a repro where long inputs (>4k) see a huge HBM bw spike and end-to-end latency double. attaching perfetto snapshot + heatmap.

maria: top-level observation: KV cache read rate jumps and we get back-to-back large memcpy kernels around the same time as the attention kernels. HBM looks saturated.

aj: can you paste the nsys command and the timeline range you captured?

maria: cmd: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o longseq_kvcache  --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi,start,end --level=full --force-overwrite --stop-on-exit ./run_infer --seq-len 8192 --batch 1`

maria: range is the 12s window where requests 140-160 land (we reproduced with the microbench harness).

liam: interesting. did you try forcing kernel selection to the fallback (no tensor cores) to see if memcpy alignment is the issue?

maria: yes, forcing non-tc kernels removes the memcpy tail but latency still high. looks like cache read storm + kernel scheduling => HBM bandwidth contention.

gita: any signs of KV page eviction/reads? maybe our prefetch window is too small for long seqs.

maria: perfetto heatmap shows frequent small KV hits but then a burst of full KV page reads. snapshot snippet: ```
KVCache::read_page  x512  0.3ms
small_gets x1024  0.02ms
full_page_load  x8  7.1ms  (HBM memcpy kernel)
```

perf-bot: automated check: model variant=M30-8192, quant=4bit, observed HBM utilization=92% during burst, avg token throughput -47% vs baseline 4096.

aj: that memcopy kernel—what's its size? might be large contiguous transfers, and NVTX shows them crossing with attention kernels.

maria: sizes ~6-12MB per page load. pattern: several small KV lookups interleaved then a few big page fills. looks like our LRU eviction triggered sequentially.

liam: could be our eviction sweep is scanning lots of entries when memory pressure hits; if eviction work runs on host thread and triggers async page fetches, those memcpy kernels can flood HBM.

gita: hypothesis: new adaptive batching heuristic increased microbatch aggregation for long sequences which increased concurrent KV working set per GPU, pushing us past the HBM threshold.

maria: i compared runs: with old batching heuristic peak concurrent KV pages ~8, new heuristic ~24. correlation looks strong.

aj: propose quick experiments: 1) cap microbatching to previous concurrent limit 2) increase prefetch window so full_page_loads happen earlier 3) make eviction randomized to avoid simultaneous sweeps.

liam: also try toggling async_prefetch=false to serialize page loads and see if that smooths bandwidth. if it reduces tail, it's scheduling contention.

maria: running experiment 1 now (cap microbatch). will push trace in ~10m.

sre-bot: FYI created alert rule 'hbm_burst_kv' with threshold 85% sustained over 3s for this customer fleet.

gita: if capping microbatch fixes it we need to add a seq-length-aware cap to batching heuristics. also add an early-warning on KV page load rate.

maria: results: cap microbatch -> HBM peak down to 64%, latency tail reduced ~30%. nvtx shows page loads are now staggered instead of concurrent.

aj: great. next steps: (a) revert adaptive microbatch for longseqs, (b) add randomized eviction delay, (c) instrument page_load start/finish counters to fire alerts.

liam: for kernel selection: consider preferring kernels with earlier completion (shorter critical path) under high HBM load even if they have slightly worse FLOP efficiency. scheduling-aware kernel selection.

gita: opened RFC draft for seq-aware batching caps + eviction jitter: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/seq-batching-evict-jitter (please review).

maria: attaching small perfetto link: https://perfetto.link/trace/ABCD1234 and the nsys output `/tmp/longseq_kvcache.qdrep` for anyone who wants to dive in.

aj: thanks, will follow up with a microbenchmark to reproduce at smaller scale and a patch for the cap + eviction jitter. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks all. labeling this thread as actionable — going to add the PRs once microbench passes.
